lines.en: It’s just before nightfall and I find myself headed to the mall with Ami and Maya.
It isn’t often that the three of us do anything without Ayane, so the air feels a little stranger than normal.
Granted, it isn’t often that Maya agrees to a plan with me involved in any form, so the entire foundation of this trip is a little out of the ordinary.
: Sensei! What’s my spending limit for today?!
I reach into my pocket and pull out...absolutely nothing.
I have no cash.
: Zero Yen.
: Zero Yen?!
: That’s even less than when you only gave me 1,000!
: Yes, that is how numbers work.
: Just give me your credit card. I checked your bank info online and it says you’re nowhere near your spending limit.
: How did you access my bank information?
: Easy. I know your email from the[school] messageboard and your password for the banking website was Boobies123.
: I am a simple man. Don’t judge.
: You’re disgusting...
Now, you’re probably wondering why I would have made something as childish as “Boobies123” my password.
And I have a perfectly reasonable explanation for that.
When I first woke up in Kumon-mi, I had a remarkably difficult time trying to access important things like my email account and bank information.
So, after some hacker-level account recovery troubleshooting (Which really just involved answering simple questions like “What is your [niece]’s name?”) I was able to get back into everything.
Then, being fed up with Internet stuff and just wanting to end the process, I changed all of my passwords to the first thing that came to mind.
Hence- “Boobies123.”
Shut up. At least I’m open about my interests.
: Shopping trip...start!
: Hooray for spending money I don’t have.
: Thanks for letting me borrow your credit card, Sensei. I’ll be sure to make it up to you when I get rich off of becoming a super-popular maid.
: I still can’t believe you are stooping to Uta’s level just for some extra spending money.
: Don’t listen to Maya. She’s just jealous because she needs to live off of her savings and is too lazy to get a job and make any money of her own.
: How is your savings account enough to live off of at your age?
: I’m good at rationing my money.
: My main strategy is choosing quantity over quality and eating large amounts of mediocre food that will last me two or three days at a time in the form of leftovers.
: Well, that’s not a bad idea...but it doesn’t sound very fulfilling.
: We can’t all have a girl who cooks and cleans for us every morning.
: Sensei, can Maya move in so she can eat with us and won’t have to ration her savings anymore?
: Are you asking me to support Maya as if she were my child?
: Ew. Don’t even joke about that.
: Is that a yes?
: What? No. Not even close.
: For once, I am actually thankful for how horrible of a person you are.
: You’re welcome, Maya.
: Oh well. Can’t say I didn’t expect you to say that.
Ami and Maya begin to look around the mall, probably figuring out which stores they want to head to first.
Just like they said yesterday, the mall is actually a bit more crowded than normal.
I guess even the lack of men around doesn’t make much of a dent in people shopping for those who are important to them.
It’s just weird to me that there are so many people around here that actually have someone important to them in the first place.
It’s kind of a bitch finding companionship in general, let alone companionship with someone of the same sex.
It’s just one of several reasons I surround myself with cute girls instead of other mysterious, glasses-wearing guys.
Why devote yourself to anything you wouldn’t also have sex with?
That’s just how I look at it.
: Huh...
: Kinda weird they don’t have any Christmas decorations up yet.
: The mall normally has lights up around this time of year. Wonder if they’re just...too busy to hang ‘em up or something?
: Don’t see how it makes much of a difference.
: Don’t say that to Ayane. She’ll hit you. That girl’s a holiday-aholic.
: That’s not even a thing.
: So, what’s your gameplan, Sensei?
: Are you gonna come with us into all of the stores and watch us try on cute winter stuff? Or are you going to go abduct another little girl and force her to wear a dog mask?
: She had an immuno-deficiency disorder...
: ...And that’s supposed to explain the dog mask?
: Poor girl never even had a chance. She’s in a better place now.
: She’s still alive...
: Only because Ami and I showed up. Who knows where you would have taken her if we hadn’t?
: Yup-yup! If you’re into dog masks, you know I wouldn’t mind-
: I’m going to stop you right there just to clarify that I am very much not into dog masks.
: Please preserve your mostly-innocent image and don’t offer to accommodate strange fetishes like that.
: Okay! I’m already kind of a fetish character in the first place, so I can see how doing more stuff like that might be over the top.
: Are you really just going to openly admit that?
: Admit what? I haven’t said anything.
: Please, for the love of the god I don’t believe in, do not turn into your [uncle].
: Maya, do you need to borrow my credit card as well?
: Wait, what?
: Is that an actual offer or are you actually insensitive enough to joke about a girl’s financial situation?
: It’s an actual offer.
: If Ami’s going to go off and buy stuff for herself, I don’t see the harm in you getting a thing or two as well.
: Oh.
: Well uhh, thanks?
: I’m okay, though. I’m not like, poor or anything. It’s fine as long as I only buy new clothes every few seasons.
: There you have it, Sensei. Does this mean I can spend extra since Maya won’t be using your card?
: Not at all. Please try to stay under 1,000 Yen total.
: I hate you and your stupid 1,000 Yen limit! I’m gonna go spend a billion Yen on stuff I don’t even need now!
: Come on, Maya!
Ami and Maya storm off and I’m suddenly left on my own without ever even having the chance to tell them I planned on coming.
It is what it is, though. I should probably buy some winter clothes myself if it’s actually going to start getting cold around here.
It’s been almost scorching every day since I was reincarnated.
For a while, I may have even thought that things were just going to stay that way forever.
But I guess a little change is good every now and then.
I wind up instinctively heading over to the store Chika works at to see if she’s in today.
Of course, it’s a Friday and[school] only ended a few hours ago, so she’s nowhere to be found.
It isn’t long before an employee I’ve never seen comes over to me and asks if I need help with anything.
: Good afternoon, Sir. Are you looking for anything in particular today?
: Yes, actually. How about a tan blonde with a ponytail and an affinity for pink?
: Ponytail?...
: Is this...a prank?
: Do I need to call security?
: No...I was just joking.
: Can you point me to where you keep all of your winter clothing? I’m thinking it’s time for a change in my life.
: I’d love to!
: Unfortunately...most of our winter stock has yet to arrive.
: All we have for men are slightly thicker shirts and-
: Good enough for me.
: Really?
: I’m not really that into fashion anyway and that sounds cheaper than anything else I’d find here.
: Oh...Well, okay then. Right this way, I suppose.
The employee leads me to a section composed entirely of blank T-shirts.
Really wanting to mix things up, I go with grey and white instead of just white and prepare to shock my students when they see me in my new casual attire.
: Oh?
I stop myself on the way out of the store after purchasing a few new shirts and find two green scarves wrapped neatly around a pair of mannequins.
: I feel compelled to buy these for some reason.
: Looking for a gift now, Sir?
The same employee from before sneaks up behind me and begins trying to sell me the scarves.
I am weak to upselling.
This is going to end poorly.
: These actually just came in this morning.
: It was so strange as well. We never ordered anything like these.
: But it’s not like I was about to just let them go to waste so...voila.
: So you’re selling things you never even ordered? How do you know how they should be priced?
: Oh, I have no idea. I just guessed.
: If you act now, I’ll let you have both for just 4,000 Yen. My regional manager is on the way here anyway so I was actually just about to take them down and hide them.
: So I’m basically the only chance you have of selling these?
: You are! And-
: I’ll give you 2,000 Yen.
: ...That’s half of the asking price.
: There is no asking price. This isn't even an item you're supposed to carry.
: 2,000 Yen or I walk.
: Fine...I guess this is my fault for revealing my secrets to you in the first place.
: Don’t beat yourself up over it. I rarely ever buy things for other people to begin with.
: This is a major victory for you.
: Sure...Right this way, Sir.
Once again, I find myself pulling out my wallet and having to use the same backup credit card I used when purchasing my shirts due to Ami having the normal one.
Then, before I know it, I’m back in the hallway carrying multiple bags, hoping to find the two girls I came here with.
: Oh! Sensei!
Ami comes running over to me, dropping a few bags of clothes she bought for herself at her feet.
Maya shows up seconds later, but with only one bag as opposed to Ami’s three.
At least I know she’d be more financially responsible if I were to ever adopt her.
: Heya! We’re basically done here.
: We’ve just gotta stop by a few other stores to get some stuff like boots and gloves and-
: Hey, whatcha got there?
: Did you actually buy yourself something for once?
: I did. I am now prepared for the cold.
: Hooray. One less thing for me to worry about.
: ...And I also got Maya here a present.
: Wait, for real?
: Why?
: I just felt like being nice.
: Are you sure?
: I wouldn’t have bought it if I wasn’t.
: Well...thank you.
: Can I see what it is?
: Sure. Go right ahead.
I hand Maya a bright green bag and she walks several steps away to check what’s inside.
Obviously, it’s nothing to be excited about, so I’m sure she’ll be back to her typical, unwavering self in a few seconds.
: Hey! What’s the big idea, mister?!
: How come Maya gets a present and I don’t?!
: Oh, did I forget to say I got you one as well?
: Here.
: Ah! Present! What is it?! What is it?!
Ami quickly snatches the bag out of my hands and looks inside of it.
: It’s just a scarf. I’m not sure if you bought one yet so, if you did, feel free to take this one ba-
: Actually, never mind. I don’t think this is returnable.
: It’s perfect! All the stuff I bought earlier was green, too!
: Maya’s is just a little bit brighter.
: I know you two planned on matching, so I hope this much is okay.
: It’s super okay! I love it!
: Maya, let me see-
: Huh?
: What’s going on?
: Maya? Are you okay?
: Yeah, I figured she'd react that way. You can just have hers as well, I guess.
: Does she really hate it that much?
: Maya, you should at least thank Sensei for going out of his way to get you a present.
: Maybe she’s not feeling okay?
: This...
: This is a joke...right?
: Maya?
: Yeah. A joke. It’s a joke...
: Hahah...hahahah...
: Hahahahah! HAHAHAHHAHAH!
: Okay, now she's just being dramatic.
: Haha...hah...
: I really do...
: Have the worst luck in the world...
Ami and I stand in silence as Maya slowly but surely regains her composure and brings herself back to her feet.
She picks up the bag and holds it tightly against her chest for a few seconds.
She breathes in and shakes her head as if to wash away any semblance of uneasiness that crept onto her face over the last several minutes.
The bell around her neck jingles as she does so.
And then-
She lowers her arms and goes back to being a normal [teenage]girl.
: Ahem.
: Thank you very much for the gift.
: It was very kind of you.
: The heck? Are we just pretending none of that ever happened?
: Nothing did happen.
: I received a bag, I opened the bag, and immediately thanked Sensei.
: There were no additional steps between any of those three things.
: Uhh...there were a bunch of additional steps.
: But I know how much you hate looking weak so we can just pretend those other steps never happened, I guess.
: What other steps? I have no idea what you’re referring to.
: But that aside, do you like your present as well?
: I love it.
: They’ll go perfectly with the outfits we have planned, too.
: I was thinking the same thing.
: I’m sure you’ll look adorable.
: Heheh~ Of course I will.
: You probably won’t look half-bad yourself, Maya.
: Thanks.
: Now-
: I believe we have a few more things we still need to buy, don’t we?
I follow the two girls into a number of stores after that and watch them try on things like boots and jackets.

I receive a number of stares from passersby but it’s hard to discern whether or not they’re due to the fact that I’m the only male in what seems like the entire mall or just that I’m with two [teenage]girls.
Either way, the stares make me feel strange.
Like I’m out of place.
But that’s just the thing.
I am out of place.
I don’t belong here.
I’m just filling in for someone who does.
And until that person comes back to reclaim the life I’ve gone and ruined-
I will continue doing things to accidentally make all of the people I know cry.
That’s just the way things work here.
The rest of the night resembles bumper-to-bumper traffic on the highway in the middle of a snowstorm.
We stop and go.
Stop and go.
Stop and go and stop and go and stop and go.
And it gets annoying.
Ami keeps her head up the entire time.
But I can’t help but notice Maya slipping in and out of character whenever she’s ignored for more than ten seconds at a time.
It’s scary how different we become when we’re not sure how to feel.
And something about the way today went must have done that to her.
But last time was kind of like this too.
In the days leading up to my first time watching the world start over, Maya was angrier than normal.
Sure, she’s always had a slightly vicious personality.
But she’s more like a stray cat than a snake.
More hesitant and easily-triggered than outright evil.
Right now, the stray cat is out in full force.
It hides behind an illusion that it’s bigger than it actually is. Stronger than it actually is.
And the second something causes the cat to question that, the illusion shatters.
So, what are we supposed to do when dealing with stray cats?
That’s simple.
You just leave them alone.
You wait for the illusion to rebuild.
And pretend there was never a second where it ever went away in the first place.
: ...and then Ayane said to the cashier that she could have her fired within minutes if she wanted to!
: That sounds about right.
As I moved through the automatic doors alongside the same girl I see just seconds after waking up every morning-
I couldn’t help but notice that, for the first time-
I was being followed by a stray cat.
